subject.title: improve(android): make Wear store releases reproducible

question: Should Android release tooling continue to accept already-valid phone version-code suffixes 50–99, and if not, what explicit migration or historical-artifact policy authorizes rejecting them?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes the accepted public release identity range, but source shown in the PR does not establish whether historical 50–99 codes must remain valid or how operators migrate them safely.

options.title: Preserve legacy codes
options.body: Keep existing valid 50–99 phone codes readable for historical releases while allocating 01–49 for new paired phone/Wear releases.

options.title: Migrate explicitly
options.body: Reject legacy codes only with a documented, tested migration that proves existing release workflows and artifacts remain recoverable.

options.title: Accept fail-closed behavior
options.body: Adopt immediate rejection of 50–99 values and document the resulting operator breakage as an intentional release-policy change.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy codes
recommendation.body: Keep existing valid 50–99 phone codes readable for historical releases while allocating 01–49 for new paired phone/Wear releases.

likelyOwner.reason: The original merged Wear architecture and its versioned companion packaging boundary are the closest evidenced ownership signal.
